Professional AI Image Generation Prompt (Highly Detailed & Precise)
Prompt:
Create a masterpiece-quality, ultra-photorealistic lifestyle portrait in a 4:5 vertical composition, captured in 8K Ultra HD with extraordinary realism, premium editorial photography quality, cinematic HDR lighting, natural skin texture, and exceptional micro-detail. The image should seamlessly blend real-world photography with expressive monochrome hand-drawn sketch art, creating the illusion that the illustrated version of the subject has stepped out of her imagination onto the wall beside her.
The scene takes place inside a modern, warm-toned minimalist home with soft beige walls, polished ivory marble flooring, and elegant Scandinavian-inspired wooden furniture. On the left side of the frame is a light oak wooden cabinet with framed botanical artwork and a small green indoor plant, contributing to a calm, cozy, contemporary atmosphere. A woven jute rug occupies the foreground, enhancing the home's natural aesthetic.
The primary subject is a beautiful young South Asian woman standing naturally beside a plain wall. She has a soft oval face, warm wheatish-fair complexion, expressive dark brown eyes, delicately arched eyebrows, a small straight nose, naturally pink lips, and subtle everyday makeup. Her dark brown hair is loosely tied into a casual low ponytail with soft face-framing strands falling naturally around her cheeks.
She wears an elegant pastel lavender embroidered Indian kurta set featuring intricate white floral thread embroidery throughout the fabric. The kurta has a round neckline, full-length semi-sheer sleeves with embroidered cuffs, matching straight pants, and traditional embroidered jutti flats. Small floral earrings, a delicate gold chain necklace, and minimal accessories complete the refined ethnic look.
The woman leans gently against the wall with a shy, playful posture. Her hands are softly clasped together in front of her body, shoulders slightly raised, one leg bent backward with only the toe touching the floor, creating an adorable, feminine pose. She gazes affectionately toward the illustrated version beside her with a subtle smile, conveying warmth, innocence, and curiosity.
Occupying the right half of the composition is a large monochrome ink sketch of the same woman drawn directly on the wall. The sketch perfectly matches her hairstyle, facial features, clothing, jewelry, proportions, and overall identity while transforming her personality into a lively cartoon-style illustration. The drawing is created using expressive black ink lines, loose cross-hatching, confident brush strokes, and sketchbook-style detailing.
Unlike the real subject's reserved pose, the illustrated character is energetic and playful. She balances on one leg with the opposite leg lifted backward, sticks out her tongue mischievously, winks one eye, and raises both hands making cheerful peace signs. Around the drawing are small hand-drawn doodles including hearts, stars, sparkle icons, motion lines, and playful accent marks that enhance the whimsical personality without overwhelming the composition.
The lighting is soft natural window light from the left, producing smooth shadows, beautiful dimensionality, realistic skin tones, subtle fabric translucency, and gentle highlights on the embroidery. The sketch should appear naturally integrated into the wall with crisp black ink contrast while remaining clearly hand-drawn rather than digitally rendered.

Concept: Seoul Summer, 1998 – Rainy Bus Stop

Prompt:

Create an authentic 15-second archival home video that appears to have been recorded in Seoul, South Korea, during the summer of 1998 using a consumer Hi8 or VHS-C camcorder. The camcorder is never visible. The audience only sees the footage captured through the camera, exactly as if watching a forgotten family videotape decades later. This is not a vlog, not a selfie, and not a cinematic film. The unseen camera operator casually documents an ordinary moment from everyday life.

The footage should faithfully recreate genuine late-1990s analogue camcorder characteristics: soft 480i resolution, subtle VHS tape grain, faint interlacing, mild colour fading, occasional autofocus breathing, slight exposure shifts, gentle handheld shake, imperfect framing, tiny zoom corrections, realistic motion blur, analogue colour bleed, and faint tape hiss. No HDR, no digital sharpening, no beauty filters, no stabilisation, no cinematic lighting, no slow motion, and no modern camera effects.

A light summer rain has just begun in a quiet Seoul neighborhood. A young Korean woman in her early twenties waits at a simple city bus stop beneath a clear plastic umbrella. She wears a pale blue oversized T-shirt tucked into relaxed-fit blue jeans, classic white sneakers, and carries a canvas shoulder bag, perfectly matching authentic Korean street fashion from 1998. Around her, commuters quietly wait while late-1990s Korean buses, sedans, and bicycles pass by on the wet street. Handwritten Hangul shop signs, overhead utility wires, convenience stores, and low-rise apartment buildings create an unmistakably authentic Seoul atmosphere.

As the rain becomes slightly heavier, a small orange tabby cat runs from beneath a parked car toward the bus stop. The woman notices it, crouches down with a warm smile, and gently shelters the cat under her umbrella. The cat calmly sits beside her while several nearby commuters smile at the unexpected moment. A city bus approaches in the background, its headlights reflecting across the rain-soaked road. The woman looks toward the arriving bus, softly laughs, gives the cat one gentle pat, and steps aboard as the doors close. The camera remains outside, lingering for a few seconds on the rainy street as the bus slowly drives away before the recording ends abruptly, exactly as if someone simply pressed the stop button on the camcorder.

Generation Requirements: Produce one continuous, uninterrupted 15-second recording with no cuts or transitions. Every detail must accurately recreate Seoul in 1998, including clothing, hairstyles, architecture, vehicles, signage, weather, and everyday behavior. Human movement must be completely natural with consistent facial identity, realistic anatomy, authentic hand movements, believable crowd interactions, and subtle environmental details such as rain, passing traffic, distant conversations, bus engine sounds, birds, and ambient city noise. Avoid AI artifacts, duplicated pedestrians, warped limbs, floating objects, unnatural expressions, perfect symmetry, or anything suggesting the footage was AI-generated. The finished result should be indistinguishable from genuine late-1990s home camcorder footage discovered in a family archive.

whoever leaked this has bigger balls than sense

two researchers replaced $7,500 of human grading with $77.81 of model calls, and the number that fell out should stop anyone shipping an agent this week: the judge disagrees with itself 13.6% of the time

it also prefers whichever answer it saw first, 72% of the time. cross-judge agreement is a kappa of 0.51: the statistical polite word for guessing

this is Eval Engineering, the layer that arrives after loops and graphs, and it installs into the agent you already pay for:

- run every comparison both ways and average the two, because one production judge picked whichever answer sat in the first slot 72% of the time
- stop shipping on a single verdict: recovering the reference answer took 11 repeated trials before a majority vote landed it, and 15 on the questions that actually mattered
- report the chance-corrected agreement instead of raw match, since the gap between those two ran 33 to 41 points on the same benchmark
- never let a model grade its own family, because self-preference tracks capability upward rather than falling away as models improve
- test stability and bias together, since two judges already running in production held above 0.95 on repeat while carrying severe positional preference
- freeze the rubric wording and version it, because semantically identical templates flipped the majority outcome in a quarter of tested cases
- write the rubric as one observable pass condition rather than a bundle of scores, so a coin-flip preference cannot hide inside an average
- let plain code take every objective call, did the test pass, does the file exist, did the state change, and leave the judge only what genuinely needs reading
- make the verdict do something structural to the run in flight, reject the handoff, swap the node, quarantine the branch, or you have built a dashboard

the catch is that your judge is a measurement instrument nobody calibrates: single-trial judging is too noisy for anything you would stake money on, and the same judges reordered by as much as 14 positions depending on which benchmark you asked

so the loop has to converge on the spec rather than on the score, because optimise against a judge long enough and the agent learns to look right instead of being right

It's not time to slow down but to accelerate!

The recent AI-powered cyberattacks have everyone talking about the risks of AI. We should. But let's not lose sight of the bigger picture!

If we work hard at it, AI will make the world safer, not less safe, just as most major technologies have.

We've already seen a glimpse of that: we defended ourselves with AI (more specifically an open model). The same systems that helped stop an AI-powered cyberattack can now help defend against millions of cyberattacks every day, while helping us identify and fix vulnerabilities before attackers exploit them.

To get there, we need three things in my opinion:

- Increase transparency with mandatory trace sharing and incident disclosure for agent cyber-attacks
- Keep AI-powered cyberattacks illegal, with meaningful penalties to disincentivize them
- Equip defenders with the best AI, especially open models, to reduce the asymmetry of capabilities between attackers and defenders

If we get those three things right, AI won't just create new cybersecurity challenges, it will make cybersecurity fundamentally and meaningfully stronger. 

And that's before considering AI's impact on science, healthcare, education, productivity, and much more.

It's not time to slow down but to accelerate!

A $0.11 CHARACTER JUST DID WHAT A $3,500 COMMISSION USED TO TAKE WEEKS TO DELIVER

Neuro-sama held 162,459 paid subscriptions at the January count roughly double those of the next human streamer

I assumed the machinery behind that was a private research lab
It's just stock VTube Studio with volume-driven lip sync and about 15 rigged animations wired to emotion hotkeys. That’s the entire visible layer

The face is the most expensive part of every VTuber project
Rigging alone costs around $100 for a bust and $500–$1,200 for premium full-body work

So I automated it

One AI-generated image, layer decomposition on a rented GPU, rigged and animated model output including hair physics, honest blinks and a painted mouth. Total cost: $0.11

The industry rig format is proprietary. Nobody has ever generated one from scratch
So instead, I shipped an open format JSON plus PNG layers, readable in any text editor

The real test was an AI agent that had never seen the project before, which was connected to the factory and asked to describe a character in one sentence
Eleven minutes and eleven cents later, the character was standing in the app, blinking and talking

Both repositories are currently free and open under an MIT licence
